cases.name: US railroads · 1873

risk.direct: Railroad shareholders faced falling equity values; railroad bondholders and lending banks faced defaults and refinancing failures. Recoveries depended on the security and reorganization, so the stock-price index is not a bondholder loss estimate.
risk.transmission: Railroad funding difficulties contributed to Jay Cooke & Co. suspending payments on September 18, 1873. Loss of confidence spread to other banks and depositors, disrupting withdrawals, credit, and payments; business failures and unemployment transmitted the shock beyond securities holders.
risk.public: Workers, households, and businesses bore wider economic disruption. These sources do not establish a comprehensive taxpayer-loss total or a public/private share of losses; neither is estimated here.
risk.timingNote: The chart reference is the April 1872 monthly price peak. The September 1873 panic is a separately labeled event 17 months later. The 1868–1878 comparison window reaches its later trough in June 1877; the short ±24-month chart stops before that trough.
risk.interpretation: Historical exposure/transmission account, not a quantified loss-allocation model or proof of fundamental overvaluation.

research.label: One-month drawdown crossing — research model estimate

protocol.status: Frozen before first model fit and test evaluation in this task; retrospective research, not a historical preregistration
protocol.target: At observation month t, conditional P_t > 0.8 * max(P_{t-11},...,P_t), forecast Y_{t+1}=1 if P_{t+1} <= 0.8 * max(P_{t-11},...,P_t). The threshold is frozen at t. Repeated crossings after recovery are possible; this is not a unique crash or bubble label.
protocol.horizon: One next monthly observation; no intramonth minimum, no two-year eventual crash claim
protocol.training_population: 49 value-weighted US industry total-return indices; every eligible month, not selected run-ups
protocol.fit: Pooled logistic regression; standardization fitted on train only; unpenalized intercept, L2 slopes, mean log loss plus lambda/2 * squared slope norm; no class reweighting, feature selection, probability clipping, or test recalibration
protocol.embargo: 1985-1986 and 1998-1999 target months excluded; feature/label history cannot overlap across retained adjacent partitions
protocol.selection: Smallest development Brier score, ties favor first candidate; retain original train-fit weights, do not refit on development
metrics: year block bootstrap CI for paired Brier improvement
protocol.uncertainty: 2000 whole-calendar-year bootstrap draws over test years, retaining all industries together; approximate intervals do not account for cross-year persistence or model selection
protocol.case_display: Every month from 24 months before each named peak through 12 months after; ineligible months null, never assigned zero. Named examples are selected retrospectively and not the performance denominator.
protocol.current_AI: Chips, Hardw, Softw are broad proxies, not AI-specific. Last available FF month July2026 predicts August2026, not current September2026.
protocol.interpretation: Estimated conditional drawdown-crossing probability under fitted historical industry model. Not a probability of fundamental overvaluation, bubble existence, or an AI crash. External asset mean-price transfer is uncalibrated. Current revised data do not establish point-in-time tradable history.
protocol.literature_scope: Returns, volatility and price path are literature-informed predictors; this one-month target and model are original research design, not a replication of Greenwood et al.'s longer-horizon crash tests. Retrospective knowledge in the literature prevents treating this as a prospectively untouched historical experiment.
